title: 100-employee strategic pivot
description: A mid-stage company announces a strategic pivot from B2C to B2B. 100 employees across PM, Eng, Sales, and Ops react. Track sentiment, intent-to-leave, and cross-functional clustering.

classes.name: PM
classes.proseIdentity: A product manager. Skeptical of pivots, but mission-driven. Cares about whether the new strategy is coherent.

classes.name: Engineer
classes.proseIdentity: A software engineer. Values clarity and execution. Tolerates pivots if the work is interesting; bristles at thrash.

classes.name: Sales
classes.proseIdentity: A salesperson. Pragmatic, quota-driven. Worries about pipeline and re-trained pitches.

classes.name: Ops
classes.proseIdentity: An operations leader. Wants the org to function; willing to support pivots if the plan is real.

payload.text: The CEO announces a pivot from B2C to B2B over the next two quarters.
All-hands Q&A surfaces concerns about cross-functional alignment.

readmeMd:
# 100-employee pivot

The interesting question: does Sales come around once the first B2B win lands at tick 60, or has the cross-functional fabric already torn?
